title: The Desperate Man

image.credit: collection not stated on source page; via arthistoryproject.com

altText: A close portrait of a young man with wide, staring eyes and hands pulled against his head, set against a dark background.

source.museum: collection not stated on source page
source.verifiedBy: arthistoryproject.com artwork page text (title, years, medium, public-domain statement); collection not stated on the page

context: An oil painting on canvas by the French artist Gustave Courbet, dated 1844 to 1845 on its source page, which tags it Portraits and Self-portraits. The page does not state the collection, and Courbet is widely known as a leader of Realism.

descriptions.k: Look at this man's face. His eyes are wide open and his hands are near his head. What big feeling could he have? Try making his face.
descriptions.g12: Gustave Courbet painted a face close up. The eyes are wide and the hands are by the head. The background is dark. The page says it may be a self-portrait. What feeling do you see?
descriptions.g35: Gustave Courbet painted The Desperate Man between 1844 and 1845. The man's wide eyes and raised hands show a strong feeling, and the dark background makes his face stand out. The page tags it as a portrait and a self-portrait. Why might a painter study his own strong expression?
descriptions.g68: The Desperate Man (1844-1845) by Gustave Courbet is a close-up portrait tagged on its page as a self-portrait. The wide eyes, the hands at the head and the dark ground concentrate attention on expression. Courbet was later a leader of Realism. How do framing, light and gesture communicate emotion, and how does a painter perform as both artist and subject?
descriptions.g910: Courbet's The Desperate Man (1844-1845) is an early self-portrait, tagged as such on its page, in which dramatic expression and tight framing create theatrical intensity. It comes from before the artist's mature Realism. How do eyes, hands and shadow build the effect, and how might the work be read as emotion, performance or a young painter's ambition?
descriptions.g1112: The Desperate Man (1844-1845) shows Gustave Courbet, tagged on the page as the sitter, in an exaggerated pose that blends Romantic emotion with a direct, close observation that foreshadows Realism. The title invites a story, yet the picture provides no setting. How might the painting be read as sincere confession, staged performance or a bid for attention, and what evidence limits each reading?

k.daily: Look at the man's wide eyes and the hands by his head. What big feeling could this be?
k.emotion: Can you make the same face as this man? What big feeling are you showing?
k.observation: Find his eyes and his hands. Where are they?
k.analysis: Where is his face in the picture, and what color is behind him?
k.line: Trace the curve of his arm with your finger. Which way does it go?

k.light: Where is the lightest part of his face?
k.meaning: What do you think the man is feeling?
k.culture: Courbet painted this man in France long ago. What would you tell a friend about this big-feelings face?
k.technique: The painter used paint to show a face up close. How is that different from a photo?
k.personal: What do you do when you have a big feeling?
k.critical: What would you add to the picture to help the man feel better?

g12.analysis: Why does your eye jump from the hands at his head to his wide eyes in The Desperate Man?

g35.shape: How do the shapes of the hands and head work together to show tension?

g68.color: How do the skin tones and dark surroundings affect the mood?

g910.line: How do the gestures of the arms and hands structure the composition?
g910.shape: How do the open, rounded features of the face help the expression read?
g910.color: How do the skin tone and dark ground relationship direct attention?
g910.texture: How does naturalistic painting of flesh serve a heightened, staged expression?

g910.light: How does directed light dramatize the face?
g910.meaning: How might the page's self-portrait tag change how we interpret performance versus record?
g910.culture: How does the painting relate to Romantic ideas of emotion before Courbet's later Realism, as widely understood?
g910.technique: How does painting oneself before a mirror shape what expressions can be shown?
g910.personal: What does the painting make you consider about the difference between feeling an emotion and staging it?

g1112.daily: How does the tension between sincerity and theatricality allow The Desperate Man to support competing readings of the painter's intent?
g1112.emotion: Might the emotional force belong to the face itself or to the viewer's expectations about expression? Weigh the visual evidence.
g1112.observation: Scan the transitions between skin, hair and shadow. How do these thresholds shape your reading of a fleeting expression as lasting?
g1112.analysis: How does the cropped framing produce focus while withholding context about setting or story?
g1112.line: How do the gestures of hand and arm form an emotional grammar, and how conventional is it?
g1112.shape: In what ways do the open features support legibility and risk caricature?
g1112.color: How does the color structure, with its dark ground and warm flesh, direct attention and shape tone?
g1112.texture: How does the technical finish of the flesh relate to later Realist commitments to observation?
g1112.space: How does the compressed, undefined space produce confrontation, and what does it exclude?
g1112.light: How does the strong light on the face against deep shadow in The Desperate Man feel natural or staged, and what supports your view?
g1112.meaning: How does the self-portrait tag complicate the question of who is performing and for whom?
g1112.culture: How does the painting stand between Romanticism and the Realism for which Courbet is better known, and where can we not be certain of the artist's intent?
g1112.technique: How does the use of one's own face as a model redefine the artist's role as both subject and observer?
g1112.personal: How does your habit of reading hands and faces shape your response to this young painter's pose, and does it meet or resist your expectation?
g1112.critical: What would a persuasive argument look like that the painting is primarily a young painter's self-promotion, and how would you counter it?

safety.method: Image viewed and approved by the site owner (visual review) on 2026-10-18. Earlier metadata screening: Title, medium (oil on canvas), years (1844-1845) and page tags (Portraits, Self-portraits) read from the arthistoryproject.com page text; the collection is not stated. SENSITIVE: the title and the sitter's wide-eyed, intense expression suggest distress. K-2 questions are kept gentle and playful (big feelings, making faces, what helps) and avoid the word scary; older bands discuss expression and performance. Only page text was read; the image file was not visually inspected, and a person must view it and confirm it is suitable for all ages before release.

teacherNote.context: An oil painting from 1844 to 1845 by the French artist Gustave Courbet, tagged Portraits and Self-portraits on its source page, which does not state the collection. The expression is intense; teachers may wish to preview it and frame discussion around feelings and performance.
directions: Have students use mirrors to study a strong feeling, draw only eyes and hands, then compare how gestures change the feeling.
Ask students to write one caption for the painting and discuss how different captions change how we read the face.
Discuss why artists study and stage emotions and how a picture can show a feeling without telling the whole story.
